name: Pan Ananapibut
detail: Fiscal Policy Office economist whose 2012 presentation titled "ภาษีความมั่งคั่ง" actually proposed a Korean-style property/land and building tax on housing above 5 million THB rather than a net wealth tax on total assets minus debt.

name: Sommai Phasee
detail: Finance Minister (2014–2015) who enacted the 2015 Inheritance Tax Act and Land and Building Tax Act; while frequently referred to in media as taxing the wealthy, these are inheritance and real property taxes excluded under Section 2.

name: Nitirat Sapsomboon
detail: Coordinator of We Fair Network. In his widely cited 2020 iLaw interview outlining tax funding mechanisms for universal welfare, he proposed capital gains tax (30%), progressive land and building tax, progressive inheritance tax, and cutting BOI privileges, but omitted an annual net wealth tax.

name: Somchai Jitsuchon
detail: Research Director for Inclusive Development at TDRI. While a leading academic voice on inequality and tax reform to finance pensions and child grants, his concrete proposals focus on land and building taxes, windfall taxes, capital gains taxes, and phased VAT increases, rather than an annual net wealth tax.

name: Lavaron Sangsnit
detail: Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance. Frequently cited in economic media discussing the structural flaws of the inheritance tax and noting that a net wealth tax (Wealth Tax) could be a future policy alternative; his comments represent administrative feasibility review and technical study rather than personal or institutional advocacy.

name: Pita Limjaroenrat
detail: Former Move Forward Party leader. While campaigning on the party's 2023 Progressive Welfare platform, his public statements focused broadly on welfare spending and economic revitalization; specific legislative drafting and direct defense of the net wealth tax was spearheaded by Sirikanya Tansakun and Think Forward Center, with no distinct standalone net wealth tax quote in his personal capacity.
